title: A Tesla stops in the middle lane of I-75 with a driver asleep; police arrest her for DUI
summary: Police found Kimberly Brown asleep in a Tesla stopped in I-75’s middle lane. An analyst described a possible attention-triggered stop; vehicle logs do not establish the mechanism.
account: ABC 7’s WWSB report of April 24, 2026 describes a Tesla stopped in the middle lane of Interstate 75 near Sarasota. Florida Highway Patrol officers found 37-year-old Kimberly Brown asleep behind the wheel at about 2 a.m. The station quotes Trooper Kenn Watson and reports that she was arrested for driving under the influence. The account says that she had expected Autopilot to take her home. Edmunds analyst Alistair Weaver explains the general driver-attention warning and stopping mechanism. The report does not include vehicle logs that establish the precise sequence in this car.
purpose: Autopilot's driver-attention monitoring is built to warn an inattentive driver. It brings the car to a stop if the driver does not respond. It is not designed to drive an impaired person home.
system: Tesla Autopilot, according to the reported account; the vehicle model and active configuration are unverified.

ratings.reason: An unconscious, intoxicated driver came to a stop without a crash. The sources document no injury and no collision avoided.
Other road users were exposed to a stationary car on the shoulder rather than a moving one. No incident with them is documented.

ai_role.statement: The original report describes a Tesla that had stopped while its driver was asleep. An automotive analyst explains how driver-attention warnings can lead to a stop, but vehicle data were not supplied to establish which functions operated in this event.
